title: Volume 2 Chapter 2: The Sister Cries, the Flames Do Not, and the Dagger Remains Unbroken 2
content: A familiar voice suddenly pierced my ears.
No way, how many days in a row is this?
"I've been looking for the Longdagger Couple."
"We're not going out on a hunt today."
I replied to Shara with a hint of exasperation.
We had agreed to notify each other beforehand when going out on a hunt, so it was needless to say.
Yet, for some reason, I couldn't recall having made that notification since we met.
"I know that."
Shara said with a wry smile,
"I know there aren't any adventurers who would go out hunting the day after defeating a Forest Dragon two days in a row.
No, you don't understand. Erika was all fired up to go out hunting today.
"What do you mean by looking for us?"
Erika asked as she invited Shara to our table.
Honestly, I didn't want to know.
If anything, I wanted her to leave. I wanted to be alone with Erika.
"Actually, I have something to tell you both."
Shara sat down and ordered tea from the staff.
The Bishop wants to meet you both at least once, so I thought I'd ask when would be a good time for you… What's wrong?
Shara looked at us with a puzzled expression.
It was probably because Erika and I instinctively exchanged glances.
Just yesterday, Erika and I had discussed the possibility of Shara being a spy from the Church.
Was this a good timing or a bad one?
"No, it's fine. But why did that come up?"
I asked, feeling an unpleasant premonition.
After that ridiculous celebration with that foolish idiot yesterday, Shara had gone to the orphanage, enduring the pressure that made everyone around her seem like robbers.
Wanting to be free from that pressure as soon as possible, she pressed a donation into the hands of the orphanage's caretaker, who looked annoyed by the late-night visitor.
Having somewhat sobered up, Shara decided to visit the Bishop to resolve her lingering questions.
It must have been quite a nuisance for the Bishop to be attacked by a drunken visitor at night.
According to Shara,
"I thought I’d ask why I was sent to you guys while also reporting that we defeated the Forest Dragon.
Listening to Shara, I was impressed by her unexpected talent.
This meant she was trying to convey that it wasn't anything special for her to talk about us to the Bishop.
By stating her role as if it were a matter of course, she was trying to instill the idea that it wasn't unnatural.
Moreover, she must have noticed that we were skeptical about her being sent to us.
She was even trying to gain empathy by saying, "I find it strange too."
This was quite impressive. The lack of any acting quality made me want to commend her.
In any case, Shara reported the defeat of the Forest Dragon to the Bishop.
Upon hearing that, the Bishop was reportedly very surprised and quite impressed.
There was no need for him to be impressed. I mean, was he really impressed?
Was he thinking of something sinister? Is everything alright?
Harm us? Would the Bishop harm us?
Well, that's something to think about when it happens.
I digressed, so let’s get back on track.
The Bishop, feeling grateful for our Sister's assistance, apparently thought it would be good to have a more detailed conversation.
That struck me as suspicious.
He probably wanted to say something because the enemy of the god he despises was getting a bit too cocky.
Or perhaps it was an assassination.
No, he wouldn't do that in the middle of the city.
In any case, I concluded that it was a troublesome matter.
I could see a future filled with complications, and it left me feeling disheartened.
So, was he going to harm us?
It was troublesome, but my thoughts of harming the Bishop were quickly squashed.
"If the Bishop is calling for us, we can't keep him waiting."
Erika's words meant we would meet him that very day.
As expected of Erika, decisive and quick.
It was so unexpected that I couldn't prepare at all.
The most I could do was prepare a hidden weapon in case they took our main weapons.
While Erika was eager to go today, I couldn't help but wonder what kind of person the Bishop was to respond so quickly.
Was he bored?

I felt bad for Shara, who was sweating profusely from running back and forth between the church and the dining hall, but I wanted to tell her that the Bishop should consider having a bit more dignity.
Even if I complained, the situation wouldn't change, and there we were, standing in front of the church alongside Erika and, incidentally, Shara.
My first impression was that it looked like a fortress.
As expected of the Church of Hekatai.
In case of emergencies, it was built to shelter citizens.
For the residents of this city, the threat of monsters attacking was a very real concern.
You could see that from the sturdy walls surrounding the church.
Conversely, one could also think that it was suitable for trapping those who were invited in. Was I overthinking that?
"Please, this way. I'll guide you."
Shara's face didn't seem to show any signs of plotting something.
And to my surprise, we were led to the Bishop's private chamber.
I had expected to be taken to a reception room or something, so I couldn't help but be taken aback.
Should I be on guard right from the start?
While I was pondering this, Shara opened the old, heavy door.
Beyond the door was a room filled with the scent of old paper.
"Welcome, Longdagger Couple."
Though simple, the sofa exuded a sense of weight that came from years of history.
As the Bishop stood up with a smile, he said, "It's a pleasure to meet you. I am Erika Longdagger."
Erika performed a graceful bow.
After a moment of being captivated by her appearance, I also bowed my head.
"I am Shin Longdagger, Bishop."
Someone please commend me for not showing any emotion when I called him "Bishop."
"I am Bival Bivality, the Bishop. I thank you for accepting this sudden request and for coming here today."
The Bishop's demeanor was soft, despite being the head of the Maki Komarukuro Barony's parish, and he didn't come off as arrogant at all.
In fact, he seemed overly polite towards adventurers, which might be due to my noble background.
With a kindly smile, he bowed his head, and as I looked at his grayish-blonde hair, I felt a sense of unease.
This was bad; I sensed no malice from him. Perhaps the Bishop had already made up his mind about something.
After inviting us to sit on the sofa, the Bishop prepared tea himself and sat across from us.
By the way, Shara was sitting next to me, beside Erika.
Shara, who had tried to help prepare the tea but was waved off by the Bishop, looked somewhat uncomfortable.
Seeing Shara, the Bishop's face once again bore a gentle wrinkle, reminding me of my father, who was about the same age.
Well, I hadn't seen a father figure with such a kind expression in a long time.
"About the reason for your visit today…"
The Bishop quickly got to the main topic.
Having been accustomed to the lengthy greetings, provocations, and probing exchanges typical among nobles, I found this promptness quite refreshing.
Nobles are a hassle, really a hassle.
If I wanted to fight, I would prefer to do so immediately after the greetings.
"Actually, I was the one who insisted on sending Shara to you."
Summarizing the Bishop's story, it went like this:
There were few precedents for sending Sisters or priests to unknown adventurers with little track record, especially since the recipients were adventurers from another country.
Most people thought it would be better to observe the situation first.
However, the Bishop made the decision on his own.
Having sent Shara without warning, he wanted to check in directly to ensure it wasn't a nuisance.
That was the gist of the Bishop's story.
Ignoring the finer details, it was a reasonable explanation.
From the Bishop's perspective, Erika Solnzali had come to them.
Of course, he would want to tie that connection as tightly as possible.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/QYL1oz5.jpeg
He probably understood that we were reluctant to approach the Church.
It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
And then there was Shara.
Shara was incredibly convenient.
As a Sister who struggled with healing magic, sending her to a noble adventurer was quite natural.
After all, what was expected of Sisters and priests sent to adventurers was their ability to use healing magic.
They were definitely not expected to be spellcasters of the so-called destructive magic.
The Church was known for being filled with people who devoted themselves to the training of magic, which was a mimicry of divine works.

Naturally, they were expected to have offensive capabilities, but primarily, they were expected to be proficient in healing magic, whether they belonged to the Healing Faction or the Demon Subjugation Faction.
If they couldn't use healing magic adequately, they couldn't be sent to ordinary adventurers.
However, it was only natural for noble adventurers to be able to use healing magic.
Upon further reflection, I couldn't help but wonder what the hell was going on.
When I glanced at Shara, she tilted her head with a puzzled expression.
I wanted to tilt my head too.
Shara was just the right fit for Erika, who had to quickly find a partner for a fake elopement.
If they were to send someone to a noble or former noble adventurer, there couldn't be a more suitable candidate.
No, in this case, I should say that the two of us were just the right fit as Shara's destination.
What a nuisance.
It felt like we were being burdened.
But still, what did it mean that they wanted to meet and talk directly?
I understood that they hadn't asked us to hand over our weapons, and it didn't seem like they were planning an assassination, either.
They probably knew that it was impossible to poison someone who could use body enhancement and healing magic, so it was hard to believe that this tea was poisoned.
Now, what on earth was the Bishop's objective in calling us here?
Could it be that he simply wanted to thank us for taking in Shara, who was genuinely troubled?
That seemed plausible. As I thought that, the Bishop cautiously asked,
"Um… has Shara caused you any trouble?"
The sincerity on the Bishop's face made it clear that he was genuinely worried about Shara.
And it was evident that he was seriously concerned about whether she had been a nuisance.
Even if he had other motives, he was genuinely worried.
Hey, Shara, you…
"Not at all, Bishop."
Erika replied in a calm voice.
"Shara was the one who delivered the decisive blow in the defeat of the Forest Dragon."
"Y-yes, I've heard that from Shara."
The Bishop's face twitched slightly.
Um… it's not that I doubt it, but is it true that the three of you defeated the Forest Dragon?
I mean, I don't doubt it, really.
It's just hard to believe all of a sudden.
Ah, I see.
The Bishop's objective was this.
He wanted to know our capabilities.
That was a straightforward request. The Bishop probably wanted to have a grasp of our abilities.
He couldn't fully trust Shara's report and wanted to confirm it by meeting us directly.
I didn't know how Shara had reported it, but it was unfortunate for the Bishop that he couldn't comprehend Erika's greatness.
Could he not understand with that kind face? Was his head all fluffy?
Well, it was understandable that he couldn't trust Shara's report. I wouldn't believe it either.
He probably wanted to assess whether the enemy of the god he despises was beyond their control.
That was quite unpleasant.
Even if the Church told Erika to die, she wouldn't hold a grudge against them.
I felt my teeth clench, and I gently rubbed my jaw.
Then, Erika detailed to the Bishop what happened when she defeated the Forest Dragon.
Hearing her recount how I fought was honestly a bit embarrassing, but I refrained from interrupting.
I was afraid I might grin if I let my guard down.
The Bishop's face showed surprise at times, admiration at others, and he looked proud when it came to Shara's story.
It was a perfectly normal reaction.
From a critical standpoint, he seemed to be a good listener, and his attitude appeared reasonable for drawing out information from others.
Wow, that's incredible.
Believe it or not, I used to go out on monster hunts with adventurers myself.
So when I heard from Sister Shara that the three of you defeated the Forest Dragon, a designated target no less, I thought I was being told a dream story.
I wished he had thought it was just a drunken dream of Shara's.
As I thought that, the Bishop stared intently at Shara's face.
Sister Shara, it might be unfortunate for you that you had to change your faction to the Demon Subjugation Faction.
However, please don't forget that it was fortunate for you to have formed a connection with the Longdagger Couple.
Shara hesitated for a moment before responding with a "Yes."
Seeing that, the Bishop straightened his posture and looked directly at us.
I had a very bad feeling.
"Longdagger Couple, I have something important to discuss."
A very, very bad feeling.
The double-walled city of Hekatai has faced the threat of destruction twice in the past.
The first time was about ten years after the city was built when it was attacked by a large-scale monster invasion.
The second time was sixty years ago.
According to records, humanity had pushed much deeper into the Demon Realm than they do now.
There were even plans to build a new city, so the efforts of humanity back then were genuine.
The one who raised his hand as a pioneer was the Bishop of that time.
He persuaded the current Baron of the Border, who was the grandfather of the current Baron, to launch a plan to build a fortress called the Church.

Looking back now, that plan seems overly hasty, but the momentum and passion of the city of Hekatai at that time were tremendous, and the church construction plan was executed at an astonishing speed.
Thus, the church was completed, and humanity was fired up to conquer and develop the Demon Realm.
But then, it appeared.
The Eight-Legged Three-Armed creature, the Sword Leg, the Three-Eyed monster—though it had various nicknames, it had no official name.
This was because it was a monster that had never been seen before and was never confirmed again afterward.
According to records, it was said to be a creature with a horse's lower body made of eight sword-like legs and a human-like upper body with a scorpion-like tail.
One day, it suddenly attacked the church, which had become a new frontline base for humanity.
It is said that many adventurers had gathered at the church at that time, but they were trampled by that single monster, suffering great losses.
Records indicate that about half of the adventurers died.
For adventurers who ventured to the front lines of the Demon Realm to die because of just one monster is a testament to its absurdity.
The fact that there were significant casualties among those adventurers alone was a disaster, but the calamity didn't end there.
In response to its attack, a large number of monsters overflowed from the forests of the Demon Realm.
The horde of monsters quickly traversed the territory humanity had opened up and reached the city of Hekatai.

To cut the details short, the fierce battle in the city of Hekatai lasted for months, and ultimately, after suffering tremendous losses, the eight-legged monster was defeated, and with the arrival of the knight order alliance from the Faltarl Kingdom and the Orukra Kingdom, humanity barely achieved victory.
The damage from this attack was immense, and while humanity healed from the wounds, it is said that they lost all the territory they had opened up in the Demon Realm.
"That church still exists in the forests of the Demon Realm."
Once Bival Bishop finished his long story, he said that.
When he began his serious tale, I wondered what it was about, but it seemed we were finally getting to the main topic.
To be honest, I really didn't want to hear this, and I would prefer to leave with Erika right now.
Whatever he was going to say, I could only imagine trouble.
The Bishop at that time did not seek to build the church out of a whim.
As proof, the church there still houses a Sacred Artifact, even now.
The words that came out of Bishop Bival's mouth were outrageous.
So suddenly and so matter-of-factly stated that I almost let it slip by, but as I processed the information, I was left speechless.
Seeing Shara's mouth agape in shock made me realize I wasn't the only one surprised, and I regained my composure.
The idea that a Sacred Artifact was left behind in the Demon Realm was a tremendous scandal.
It was shocking that it had been hidden for sixty years, but being suddenly revealed such a significant secret was more confusing than surprising.
Surely this wasn't a parting gift from the dead.
"You understand, if this leaks out, it would be a disaster for both our Church and the city of Hekatai."
Sacred Artifacts are famous as religious symbols, but even more so as the core of Hekatai's barrier device.
The barrier created by a Sacred Artifact can maintain a powerful barrier without consuming vast amounts of magical power like other barrier devices.
"So, does that mean the current barrier of Hekatai…?"
I couldn't help but voice my question, which was more of a thought than an inquiry.
The Bishop shook his head without a hint of concern.
No, there isn't just one Sacred Artifact.
You can think of it as having installed part of it in the church.
However, the strength of the barrier seems to have weakened compared to back then.
In any case, it was not something that should leak out.
The fact that he told us this means…
"Now, to get to the main topic…"
I fought the urge to cover my ears.
"I would like you, the Longdagger Couple, to retrieve that Sacred Artifact."
The Bishop's expression was utterly serious.
This had turned into something outrageous.
Shara Ransura realized her face was turning pale.
The Bishop had started saying something crazy.
He was asking them to go to the mid-level of the Demon Realm and retrieve a Sacred Artifact that had been left behind and abandoned decades ago.
Shara understood.
This was not something that could be easily leaked.
And if that was the case, it meant that it was a request for Erika, Shin, and herself to retrieve it.
Why on earth!?
This was absurd; it was undoubtedly absurd. Hadn't she complained enough yesterday?
Those two were extraordinary, amazing.
They sometimes boasted at incomprehensible times, but they were kind and pleasant people.
And yet, to act alongside such two, she felt she was lacking in strength.
She had complained about it endlessly. Had the Bishop been a bit sleepy and misheard her?
If that was the case, it was a terrible misunderstanding.
Those two could probably hum a tune while flattening the mid-level of the Demon Realm, but with her as a burden, that would be difficult.
They were stronger without any excess baggage.
Could it be that her being sent to them was to make it easier for them to retrieve the Sacred Artifact?
If that was the case, she felt incredibly guilty towards them.
Though they had only known each other for a short time, Shara had taken a liking to them.
Now, she was putting those two in danger by taking a burden like herself into the perilous mid-level of the Demon Realm.
Shara felt dejected. More than anything, it was due to her own lack of ability.
Of course, after Shin and the others left, she had pressed the Bishop for the truth, but he simply smiled with a look of compassion and said,
"Shara will be fine.
Though he seemed full of confidence, which made her want to agree, Shara found it hard to nod.
While she felt a slight relief at having learned a bit about what he was planning, Shara realized the source of her anxiety and became even more disheartened.
Having repeatedly told herself that she was lacking in strength to accompany those two…
What on earth, am I in my right mind? Shara questioned her sanity.
Did those two consider her a companion?
That was what worried her.
"I'm sorry, because I spoke about you two to the Bishop, this has turned into a huge problem."
With a downcast expression, Shara said this the day after being asked by Bishop Bival to retrieve the Sacred Artifact.
It was in the library of the Adventurer Guild, where she had gone to search for materials on the Demon Realm.
Erika turned around after returning a book she had pulled halfway from the shelf.
"You don't need to worry about it, Shara."
Saying this, Erika gently took Shara's hands in hers and smiled.
Her red hair swayed gently under the light of the magical tools.
"We have a purpose, and the request from the Church aligns with that, so it's not a nuisance."
As she said this, Erika sought my agreement with just a glance.
I held back a sigh that almost escaped and replied, "Yeah, that's true."
Indeed, Erika had accepted the request from Bishop Bival right then and there.
This surprised Bishop Bival as well; he probably thought she would either make some excuse to decline or delay her response.
By the way, I was also quite surprised.
When I got home and asked why she hadn't turned down the request, she replied that it was the way of adventurers to challenge danger, which was a very cool response.
As expected, the person I like is amazing.
She's beautiful and cool.
Additionally, Erika was adventuring with the goal of raising her adventurer rank.
Completing a request from the Church would indeed significantly increase her credibility.
She had mentioned wanting to raise her adventurer rank before, and while I thought she was still pursuing that goal, it was just a passing thought.
According to Erika, "I shall ensure you attain a rank befitting you."
In other words, it might be more about her saying that my standing is lower than hers, so I should at least raise my adventurer rank.
That was entirely true.
Standing next to Erika, even a king's status would seem diminished. Let alone mine.
That aside, while Erika's words and my own didn't completely lift Shara's downcast expression, they did make it somewhat better.
However, it truly didn't seem like acting.
Considering the situation, it appeared to be exactly as the Church planned, so it would be natural to think that Shara's demeanor was an act.
Yet, I felt no hint of pretense from Shara.
Despite being a noble, I was aware that I was not particularly good at such subtle games, but I thought I was somewhat accustomed to them.
But from Shara, I felt none of that.
For a moment, a question crossed my mind: Was Shara not acting at all? But I quickly dismissed it.
From the Church's perspective, it would be a great success to offload a dangerous request onto troublesome individuals.
They would need to venture deep into the Demon Realm, and given the nature of the request, it would have to be with a small group.
The Church likely considered the possibility of failure to be high, and if they failed, they would probably find some excuse to blame them, or even wish for their demise.
